# Direct low-sector proof from the ordinary triangle-depth envelope

This replaces the large three-variable polynomial certificate in the
low-sector triangle-chain theorem by one sharp two-parameter arithmetic
lemma. Its only polynomial positivity checks have thirteen explicitly
listed scalar Bernstein coefficients, all given below. No numerical
evidence or external coefficient file is required for the proof.

## 1. A universal ordinary triangle cap envelope

Let T=conv(0,e_1,e_2), V=area(T), and let F_(a,r)(q) be the cap area
of rT at normal (a,1-a), divided by V, with a in [1/2,1]. For q>=0,

    F_(a,r)(q) >= 4q(r-2q)_+.                            (1)

Proof. It is enough to consider 0<q<r/2. For 1/2<a<1, on the upper
proper branch the difference between the two sides is exactly

    [ar-(4a-1)q]^2/[a(2a-1)] >=0.                       (2)

On the lower proper branch r>=q/(1-a)>=2q, the difference is

    r^2-4qr+q^2[8-1/(a(1-a))].

Its derivative in r is 2r-4q>=0, so its minimum in that branch is
at r=q/(1-a). There it agrees with the nonnegative expression (2).
The empty cap branch cannot occur when q<r/2 and a>=1/2.
At a=1/2 the difference is (r-2q)^2. At a=1 it is (r-3q)^2.
The cases q=0 or q>=r/2 have a zero right side and are immediate.

For the low sector a in [1/2,2/3], at r=1 and q=1/3 there is the
additional exact bonus

    F_(a,1)(1/3) >= 1/2 = 4/9+1/18.                    (3)

Indeed this threshold is in the lower branch, so its value is
1-1/[9a(1-a)], whose minimum on this interval is 1/2.

## 2. A sharp arithmetic envelope inequality

Put t=1/3 and gamma=4/9. For 0<k<=1 and 0<=beta<=k/3 define

    W(k)=sum_(h=0)^infinity (1-kh)_+^2,
    K_-(h)=4(t-beta h)[t-(k-2beta)h]_+,
    K_+(h)=4(t+beta(h+1))[t-2beta-(k+2beta)h]_+,
    K(k,beta)=sum_(h=0)^infinity [K_-(h)+K_+(h)].

Every sum is finite. The first multiplier of K_- is nonnegative
where its positive-part multiplier is nonzero: its support endpoint
t/(k-2beta) is at most t/beta, with beta=0 interpreted directly.
Both kernel sums vanish before or at h=1/k. Thus no negative-radius
or spurious far-tail terms have been introduced.

**Arithmetic lemma.** For all these parameters,

    K(k,beta) >= gamma W(k)-4/81.                        (4)

The constant 4/81 is attained at k=2/3, beta=1/6.

### 2.1. The elementary range k>=1/2

Only h=0,1 can contribute, because the affine radius at h=2 is
nonpositive. Write r=1-k. The right h=1 kernel vanishes. Hence

    K-gamma W
      =4(t+beta)(t-2beta)_+
        +4(t-beta)(t-k+2beta)_+ - gamma(1-k)^2.           (5)

On every interval between its activation knots, the right side is
a concave quadratic in beta. Its minimum on [0,k/3] is therefore at
one of the four points

    beta=0, (k-t)/2, t/2, k/3.

All are in that interval for 1/2<=k<=1. The first gives a nonnegative
value, and the last gives zero. If k>=2/3, both middle evaluations
are at least -gamma(1-k)^2>=-4/81, since the two kernel terms are
nonnegative and 1-k<=1/3.

If 1/2<=k<=2/3, the kernel contribution at beta=(k-t)/2 is

    (2k+2/3)(2/3-k),

and at beta=t/2 it is

    (2/3)(2/3-k).

The former is no smaller. Subtracting gamma(1-k)^2 from the latter
gives a function with derivative 2/9-8k/9<0 on this interval, so
its minimum is at k=2/3 and equals -4/81. This proves (4) for this
range and verifies equality at the stated two parameters.

### 2.2. An arithmetic quadratic upper bound

For p>=0 and l>0 let S_2(p,l)=sum_(h>=0)(p-lh)_+^2. Then

    S_2(p,l)<=p^3/(3l)+p^2/2+3pl/16.                    (6)

Proof. Write p/l=N+delta, N a nonnegative integer and delta in [0,1).
The elementary sum of squares gives the exact identity

    S_2(p,l)=p^3/(3l)+p^2/2+pl/6-(l^2/3)B_3(delta),
    B_3(delta)=delta(delta-1/2)(delta-1).

For delta<=1/2, B_3 is nonnegative. Otherwise

    -B_3(delta)=delta(delta-1/2)(1-delta)<=delta/16,

because the last two factors have sum 1/2. Since l delta<=p,
the last term in the identity is at most pl/48. Adding pl/6 proves
(6), including p=0 and exact truncation knots.

We also use the linear-hinge lower bound

    S_1(p,l):=sum_(h>=0)(p-lh)_+ >=p^2/(2l)+p/2.         (7)

It follows from the trapezoid inequality for the convex function
(p-lx)_+, whose integral is p^2/(2l).

### 2.3. Integral estimates for 0<k<=1/2

Here beta<=1/6, so P=t-2beta>=0. Put L_-=k-2beta>0 and L_+=k+2beta.
The two continuous kernel integrals and their first terms are

    I_-=2t^3/L_--2beta t^3/(3L_-^2),
    I_+=2(t+beta)P^2/L_++2beta P^3/(3L_+^2),
    O_-=gamma,             O_+=4(t+beta)P.               (8)

The minus kernel is convex on [0,infinity): on its positive interval
its quadratic coefficient is 4beta(k-2beta)>=0, and its final
derivative jumps upward to zero. Thus the trapezoid bound yields

    sum_h K_-(h)>=I_-+O_-/2.                            (9)

For the plus kernel let alpha_h=(P-L_+h)_+. On its support,

    K_+(h)=2(1-kP/L_+)alpha_h-(4beta/L_+)alpha_h^2.

The first coefficient is nonnegative. Apply (7) to the first sum and
(6) to the negatively weighted second sum. The result is

    sum_h K_+(h)>=I_++O_+/2-3beta P/4.                  (10)

The integral and first-term expressions in (8) can be recovered by
collecting the two polynomial pieces in this calculation. The final
error is exactly (4beta/L_+)(3PL_+/16). When P=0 both sides of
(10) are zero, so the endpoint is included directly.

Also (6) with p=1,l=k gives

    W(k)<=1/(3k)+1/2+3k/16.                             (11)

We now prove the remaining entirely explicit inequality

    I_-+I_++(O_-+O_+)/2-3beta P/4+4/81
      >= gamma[1/(3k)+1/2+3k/16]                        (12)

for 0<k<=1/2 and 0<=beta<=k/3. Equations (9)-(11) then prove (4).

### 2.4. The scalar verification of (12)

Set v=3beta/k in [0,1], and denote the left side of (12) minus its
right side by H(k,v). Direct substitution of (8) gives

    H(k,v)=N(k,v)/[324k(2v-3)^2(2v+3)^2],

where

    N(k,v)=
      k^3(96v^6-1152v^5-432v^4+7776v^3-7290v^2)
      +k^2(-432v^5-3888v^4+9720v^3+1944v^2-8019v-2187)
      +k(-896v^4+4320v^3-3744v^2-5832v+7128)
      -768v^4+1152v^2.

The denominator is positive. Differentiating gives

    partial H/partial k
      =[k^3 P_3(v)-k^2 P_2(v)-128v^2(3-2v^2)]
          /[108k^2(2v-3)^2(2v+3)^2],                   (13)

with

    P_3(v)=4v^2[16v^4-192v^3-72v^2+1296v-1215],
    P_2(v)=144v^5+1296v^4-3240v^3-648v^2+2673v+729.

The bracket in P_3 is increasing on [0,1]: its derivative is
64v^3-576v^2-144v+1296>=576>0. Its value at 1 is -167.
Thus P_3<=0. To verify P_2>0 without an unresolved polynomial claim,
write B_j^n(v)=binom(n,j)v^j(1-v)^(n-j). Its exact Bernstein expansion
has the following SIX positive coefficients in order j=0,...,5:

    P_2(v)=sum_(j=0)^5 b_j B_j^5(v),
    (b_0,...,b_5)=(729,6318/5,8667/5,9072/5,7209/5,954).

This identity is checked simply by expanding the displayed basis.
Every term in the numerator of (13) is nonpositive, and its second
term is strictly negative. Therefore H is decreasing in k, so
H(k,v)>=H(1/2,v).

At the latter endpoint,

    H(1/2,v)=Q(v)/[648(2v-3)^2(2v+3)^2],
    Q(v)=48v^6-1008v^5-8968v^4+22248v^3
                         -4581v^2-19683v+12069.

Its exact Bernstein expansion has the following SEVEN positive
coefficients in order j=0,...,6:

    Q(v)=sum_(j=0)^6 c_j B_j^6(v),
    (c_0,...,c_6)=
      (12069,17577/2,26013/5,24237/10,2899/3,3475/6,125).

Again this is a finite explicit polynomial identity. Positivity of
the basis proves Q>0 on [0,1]. This proves (12), and hence (4) in
the small-k range. Together with Section 2.1 the sharp arithmetic
lemma is fully proved for every allowed k and beta.

## 3. Consequence for the low normal sector of actual triangle chains

Use the established deficit-monotone affine-radius reduction and
maximal-leg extension for a half-integer symmetric concave common-
vertex triangle chain at its actual central own centroid. The only
remaining case has an affine maximal leg r_h=1-kh>0 with
0<k<=1 and 0<=beta<k/3, and a in [1/2,2/3]. Its two actual cap
thresholds are q_h=t-beta h and p_h=t+beta(h+1).

Apply the universal triangle envelope (1) at every ORIGINAL fiber.
Its two contributions are exactly K_-(h),K_+(h), as defined above;
their supports occur before the radius becomes negative. At the
base-zero own fiber use the additional bonus (3), without altering
any other term. The normalized actual cap therefore satisfies

    J >= K(k,beta)+1/18
      >= gamma W(k)+1/18-4/81
       = gamma W(k)+1/162.                              (14)

Since the original total normalized mass is 2W(k), this proves the
desired constant gamma/2=2/9, with strict surplus for the maximal
affine leg in this remaining sector. The exact prefix-extension
argument excludes every violating finite affine leg, and the exact
deficit-monotone replacement excludes every violating original
concave chain. The pairwise proof covers beta>=lambda/3, including
lambda=0. Zero terminal radii add zero area and are deleted exactly.

The all-positive normal sector a>=2/3 is treated by the independent
high-sector theorem (or the newer all-dimensional counting proof).
The archived positive-normal reduction and paired tilt comparison
then give all closed ambient halfspaces for this restricted symmetric
triangle-chain theorem. Throughout, the selected center is one
actual base-zero point, all caps keep one shared beta, and the
mixed-integer mass is the exact finite sum on its original fibers.
